title: Operational Controls and Request Templates: Access, Changes, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel
author: Aditi Rao
body:
Summary
--------
This playbook collects company-wide operational controls and standardized request templates for common cross-functional processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding/management, and travel reimbursements. The goal is to provide a single, actionable reference for requesters, approvers, and operational owners to reduce friction, accelerate approvals, and ensure compliance with security and finance controls.

Audience and scope
------------------
- Audience: all Redwood employees, managers, approvers, IT, security, finance, and procurement partners.
- Scope: applies to host-based and cloud access, configuration changes to production and infra, data classification and retention decisions, purchase orders and expense flows, third-party vendor relationships, and business travel booked on company funds. Exclusions: specialized customer contracts (see finance-legal).

High-level principles
---------------------
1. Least privilege by default. Grant the minimum access required and set expirations.
2. Segregation of duties. Requester, approver, and implementer should be different where practical for privileged actions.
3. Evidence-first approvals. Approvals should include justification and relevant risk mitigations.
4. Standardized templates and SLAs. Use the templates below to ensure consistent triage and predictable processing times.
5. Risk-based exceptions. Temporary exceptions require documented compensating controls and explicit approval by Security or Finance depending on domain.

Section A — Access & Permissions
--------------------------------
Purpose: Define how employees request, approve, and audit access to systems, data stores, and vendor consoles.

Access types and owners
- Identity (Corp Google/SSO): People Ops (onboarding/offboarding lifecycle).
- Cloud console & infra (AWS/GCP/Azure): Cloud Platform team (eng-infra) + Security for privileged roles.
- Production service access (SSH, SRE Consoles): Eng SRE (eng-sre) and service owners.
- Data access (analytics warehouse, S3 buckets): Data Platform + Data Security.
- Third-party vendor consoles: Procurement + Security.

Request process (standard flow)
1. Requester fills the Access Request template (see template A).
2. Request routes to the manager and the resource owner for approval.
3. Security reviews high-privilege requests (see privilege thresholds).
4. Provisioning is executed by Cloud Platform or delegated delegation owners.
5. Access records automatically expire as requested; tickets are created for renewals.

Privilege thresholds requiring Security review
- Any role granting admin/root in production services.
- Access to data classified as Confidential or Restricted (see data classification).
- Permanent cross-org role grants (e.g., org-wide billing).

Access audit cadence and responsibilities
- Quarterly automated access review for all privileged roles (Owner: Security).
- Managers must attest to team access lists on employee promotions and role changes (Owner: People Ops).

Template A: Access Request (copy into ticket system)
```
Title: [Short] Access Request: <Resource> for <User>
Requester: <Name / Email>
Manager: <Name / Email>
Resource owner: <Service / Team>
Purpose: <Business reason and duration>
Role requested: <role name / scope>
Expiration: <date or 90 days default>
Compensating controls (if any): <MFA, jump box, audit hooks>
Security review required: yes/no
```

Section B — Change Management
-----------------------------
Purpose: Ensure controlled, auditable, and low-risk changes to production systems, infra, and tenant-facing routing.

Change categories
- Routine (non-impacting config that can be automated): fast-track via CI/CD with tests and monitoring.
- Standard (pre-approved, repeatable ops tasks): documented runbook and approved cadence.
- Major (config, schema, or infra changes with potential service impact): requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) review.
- Emergency (outage mitigation): post-hoc documentation required within 24 hours.

Approval matrix (summary)
1. Routine: implementer + automated gates. SLA: immediate.
2. Standard: team manager + service owner. SLA: 2 business days.
3. Major: service owner + infra lead + CAB (Security, SRE, Product). SLA: 5 business days for scheduled window.
4. Emergency: engineer + oncall lead; CAB post-facto review.

Change request template
```
Title: Change Request: <Service> - <Short desc>
Requested by: <Name>
Impact: <low/medium/high>
Rollout plan: <steps, smoke tests>
Rollback plan: <steps>
Monitoring and success criteria: <metrics to watch>
Change window: <date/time>
Approvers: <list>
Risks & mitigations: <list>
```

Pre-deployment checklist (required for Major)
- Run unit/integration tests in staging.
- Load test if change affects performance-critical paths.
- Notify downstream teams and schedule oncall coverage.
- Create automated alerts and dashboards (SLO error budget guardrails).

Section C — Data Management and Classification
---------------------------------------------
Purpose: Provide a simple taxonomy for data handling, retention, and approved storage locations.

Data classification table
| Classification | Examples | Storage requirements | Access rule |
|----------------|----------|----------------------|-------------|
| Public | Marketing pages, public docs | Any public cloud bucket with public-read | No restrictions |
| Internal | Internal docs, Slack history | Encrypted corp storage | Manager-approved, least privilege |
| Confidential | Customer PII, contractual docs | Encrypted at-rest and transit; limited to vault-backed stores | Requires Data Owner + Security approval |
| Restricted | Health data, regulated datasets | Air-gapped or VPC-only, HSM/KMS-backed keys | Requires Data Owner + Legal + Security approval |

Retention and deletion
- Default retention: 3 years for Internal, 7 years for Confidential unless otherwise specified by Legal.
- Data deletion requests must include dataset path, owner, justification, and cross-checks to backups. Data Platform executes deletion and logs actions.

Data access approval process
1. Determine classification.
2. Use Access Request template and mark as Confidential/Restricted when required.
3. Data Owner and Security approve; Data Platform provisions view- or copy-only access where feasible.

Section D — Procurement & Expenses
----------------------------------
Purpose: Standardize approvals, thresholds, and required documentation for purchases and reimbursements.

Spend thresholds and approvers
- < $1,000: Requester + Manager.
- $1,000 - $10,000: Requester + Manager + Budget owner (Product/Finance).
- > $10,000: Requester + Manager + Finance Director approval + Procurement review.
- Annual contracts > $100,000: Procurement + Legal + VP signoff.

Required documentation for purchases
- Business justification and expected ROI or use-case.
- Vendor quote and SOW (if applicable).
- Cost center and GL code.
- Security assessment checklist for SaaS vendors (if the product processes company or customer data).

Template B: Purchase Request (PO initiation)
```
Title: Purchase Request: <Vendor> - <Product>
Requester: <Name>
Cost center: <code>
Amount: <$X>
Business justification: <short>
Vendor contact & SOW: <link>
Security assessment: <completed/skip>
Billing cadence: <monthly/annual>
Desired vendor start date: <date>
Approvals required: <list>
```

Expense reimbursement rules
- Use corporate card where possible. If personal card used, submit expense within 30 days with receipts.
- Per diem caps: domestic $75/day, international $125/day (exceptions require manager approval).
- Hotel: book standard room; upgrades allowed with manager pre-approval.

Section E — Vendor Onboarding & Management
-----------------------------------------
Purpose: Ensure consistent risk assessment, contract terms, and operational controls for third-party providers.

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum)
1. Business owner identifies need and budget.
2. Procurement collects vendor profile and references.
3. Security completes initial security questionnaire (applicable for SaaS/files/data access).
4. Legal reviews contract terms and data processing addenda (DPA) if PII is involved.
5. Finance establishes payment terms and GL codes.
6. Vendor access: provisioned as least-privilege and time-limited.

Ongoing vendor controls
- Quarterly vendor risk review for high-impact vendors (Owner: Procurement + Security).
- Contract renewals flagged 90 days before expiry.
- Incident playbook and notification timelines must be in contract for data-impacting vendors.

Template C: Vendor Intake Summary
```
Vendor name: <vendor>
Business owner: <team>
Service provided: <description>
Data scope: <none/customer/employee>
Security tier: <low/medium/high>
Contract term: <months>
Primary contact: <name/email>
Key SLAs: <availability, RTO>
```

Section F — Travel Policy (business travel)
------------------------------------------
Booking and approval
- All business travel requires a Travel Request (Template D) and manager approval before booking.
- Use corporate travel vendor or approved booking tool to capture company rates.

Per diems and allowable expenses
- Domestic meals: up to $75/day (receipts optional under per diem).
- International: up to $125/day.
- Ground transportation: economy rideshare or taxi; car rental: compact only unless pre-approved.

Safety and duty of care
- Employees must share itinerary and emergency contact with People Ops when traveling internationally.
- Company-provided travel insurance covers medical evacuation for approved trips; People Ops must be notified for high-risk regions.

Template D: Travel Request
```
Traveler: <Name>
Purpose: <meeting/conference>
Dates: <start - end>
Destination: <city/country>
Estimated cost: <USD>
Manager approval: <Name>
Health & safety notes: <any restrictions>
```

Section G — Internal Templates and Automation Tips
--------------------------------------------------
- All templates above should be copied into the ticketing system (Jira/ServiceNow integration) and configured with appropriate routing and SLAs.
- Where possible, use ephemeral credentialing (e.g., AWS STS, short-lived tokens) and automation for provisioning to reduce manual work and expiration drift.
- Integrate access and change requests with audit logs and email/SMS alerts for high-severity events.

Exception and waiver process
---------------------------
1. Submit an Exception Request (same format as corresponding template plus \"Compensating Controls\").
2. Exceptions are limited to 30 days by default. Longer exceptions require escalation to Security or Finance and documented compensating controls.

Operational SLAs and metrics to track
- Access requests: 90% handled within 2 business days.
- Change requests (Major): 95% scheduled within 7 business days.
- Procurement PO creation: 95% within 3 business days for approved requests.
- Vendor review cycle completion: 100% for high-impact vendors within 30 days of intake.

Roles and ownership table
- People Ops: onboarding/offboarding, travel approvals, per diem policy owner.
- Security: privileged access review, data classification owner for Confidential/Restricted, security questionnaire.
- Procurement: vendor onboarding, contract lifecycle, high-value negotiations.
- Finance: spend approvals, PO issuance, GL coding and expense policy.
- Cloud Platform / Eng-SRE: provisioning, change implementation, runbook maintenance.

FAQ (short)
Q: Who can approve a tool purchase for developer productivity at $2,500?
A: Requester + Manager + Budget owner. If the vendor stores customer data, add Security review.

Q: How to request access to a customer dataset labeled Restricted?
A: File an Access Request and select "Restricted" classification; obtain Data Owner + Legal + Security approvals.

- 2025-02-03: Added Procurement thresholds and Travel per diem updates.

Contact and escalation

- For urgent security or vendor incidents, follow the Incident Response playbook in /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.
